name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v3338: The second eye read v3336 and found TWO more false negatives in the git half, the direction that banks a version mid-grade. MEASURED, 2 of 6 wrong. ONE, AND IT IS FIXED: v3336 skipped any token starting with a dash but never consumed the VALUE of the flags it knows take one, so git minus C log push read the DIRECTORY named log as the subcommand, matched it in the takes-push-as-an-argument list and answered False on a real push. v3336 dropped value-consumption on purpose, because the flag list can never be complete, but the remedy for that was the scan-onward fallback and not blindness to the flags we DO know. Both now work together: a known value-flag consumes its value, and an unknown bare token, which is what an unlisted flag value looks like, simply keeps scanning. TWO, AND IT IS A STATED LIMIT RATHER THAN A DEFERRED BUG: an ALIAS cannot be seen from a command line at all. git with a dash c alias.p equals push and then p runs a push and reads as False here, because nothing in the argv says what p expands to. Resolving it would mean running git config, a second process on every liveness check, and the flock signal covers that window. It is written into the docstring so the next reader does not rediscover it as a defect. TWO FURTHER FINDINGS WERE REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT: a ref whose basename is push, and a worktree subcommand missing from the list, both returned the SAFE answer on test rather than the one predicted. Re-measured across 16 cases: 0 wrong, the alias still False by design, and a free tree still answers free. 6 red-proofs PROVEN.
